History & Physical (Detailed)

Consult Summary:
50-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and hypertension presents with a 5–6-day history of persistent dry cough and rhinorrhea, associated with chills, myalgias, and fatigue—clinical picture most consistent with a self-limiting viral upper respiratory tract infection; symptomatic care advised and safety-net provided.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Continuous dry cough (day and night) for 5–6 days.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Rhinorrhea since onset.  
  – Chills/shivering in bed; subjective fever (temperature not taken).  
  – Myalgias (arms, legs, generalized) and lethargy.  
  – Transient diarrhea at illness onset (resolved).  
  – Throat irritation attributed to coughing; no true odynophagia.  
  – No sputum production, chest pain, dyspnea on ordinary activity, ear pain/discharge, nausea, vomiting, rash, or urinary symptoms.  
• Course: Symptoms began simultaneously; diarrhea resolved, cough persists and interferes with sleep.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None specified; cough worse at night; no specific relief.  
• Review of systems: As above; appetite preserved; no significant weight change noted.

Past Medical History:
• Type 2 diabetes mellitus – under primary care follow-up.  
• Hypertension – controlled on medication.

Medications:
• Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Lisinopril – dose/route/frequency not documented.
Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives with partner; partner asymptomatic.  
• Occupation: IT developer; largely sedentary work.  
• Smoking: Former smoker; quit ~6 months ago.  
• Alcohol: Wine on ~3 evenings/week, 2–3 glasses per occasion (below but close to recommended limits). Counselor advised reduction to ≤2 glasses/week with goal of eventual cessation.  
• Exercise: Occasional Pilates; currently limited by myalgias.  
• No notable psychosocial stressors reported.

Family History:
• Father with type 2 diabetes.  
• No other relevant familial illnesses reported.

Physical Examination:
Not performed (telephone/virtual consultation); no vitals provided.

Investigations:
None ordered or available.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected viral upper respiratory tract infection (likely common cold/viral bronchitis).
  • Reassurance; typical course 7–10 days.  
  • Symptomatic management: adequate rest, maintain hydration, regular Paracetamol as needed.  
  • Advise 1–2 days off work to rest and reduce transmission risk.  
  • Safety-net: return in 2–3 days if no improvement or sooner if worsening (persistent fever, increasing cough, new dyspnea, chest pain); may consider chest exam and antibiotics if bacterial superinfection suspected.

Issue 2: Chronic conditions (type 2 diabetes, hypertension).
  • Continue Metformin and Lisinopril as prescribed.  
  • Reinforce lifestyle measures: alcohol reduction per above, smoking abstinence, routine follow-up with primary care for monitoring BP and HbA1c.

General Plan items:
  • Encourage gradual return to normal activity as tolerated.  
  • Advise partner to monitor for symptoms; standard hygiene measures.  
  • Follow-up: routine diabetes/hypertension visits as scheduled; acute re-review if red-flag symptoms emerge.

Quality checks:
• Missing/expected elements: No vitals or physical examination findings obtained; medication doses/frequencies not documented; immunization status (e.g., influenza, COVID-19) not addressed.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal background noise.
